scope: Isolated Chromium pointer/keyboard integration, actual HTTP handlers and encrypted repository over pg-mem; not production consent or live acceptance

added_cases.valid_run: Advance browser time 181 seconds before selecting the retained run. Human fixture approval reaches the actual handler and encrypted ledger once; exact run is accepted and restored with polling, unchanged deadlines and one row.
added_cases.expired_run: Advance browser time 181 seconds, expire the isolated server run, then approve through pointer/keyboard. Actual handler returns 409 pairing_environment_unavailable; zero ledger rows and zero grants.
added_cases.database_boundary: Only the production eligibility module's database dependency is replaced in the test bundle. Its actual SQL and validation execute against isolated pg-mem tables. No production entrypoint or consent bypass is added.
added_cases.limits: Browser clock expiry models loss of the presence-derived prop; it is not a live supervisor or EXE restart. Runtime reconstruction and injected fixture provider identity are not actual provider delivery or human consent.

initial_test_observation_failure.description: Expired-run cases observed HTTP 409 but timed out reading Chromium's error response body. The test now captures the actual handler body before forwarding its unchanged response.

unresolved_recovery_boundary: The expired-run denial shows generic reconciliation guidance and freezes the submitted selection. These tests prove rejection, not a complete path to another reviewed run. Any release of an uncertain request must prevent a late or previously committed issuance from creating duplicate authority.
